tasks.scope: The dispatch readiness reader (bin/session-probe.py) recognises the idle footer of codex-cli 0.170.0, with fixtures in tests/dispatch/current-readiness-footer.test.ts. Limit: two reader gaps stay open under this task and are not in this candidate: a Codex working screen and a footer row that wraps onto a second line are not recognised.

Opt-in units integrated from the local workspace line, each inert unless its setting is given: a per-launch opt-out of the automatic cmux worker restart and two settings that keep the workspace host and the reconciler from taking the operator's screen (bin/lib/workspace-host.sh, src/reconciler/cli.ts, docs/setup/worker-focus.md); on macOS, a setting that gives a confined Codex worker the OS-shipped CA bundle file (src/session/worker-sandbox.ts); regression tests for the single-attempt submission argv of the dispatch caller and for bounded screen reads and the readiness budget. Limit: the control workspace itself is not switched to this line by the release; local-only documents of that line are not included.

Instruction text only (tooling/instructions/common.md): every machine runs a controller session with the same id, a bare id is ambiguous across machines, and how to address the local and the remote one. Limit: no tool changes its addressing in this candidate; the resolver change is a telepty task.

The package no longer declares a dependency on @dmsdc-ai/aigentry-telepty, so installing it no longer installs a nested telepty whose install script could replace a newer running daemon. The telepty requirement is stated by capability at init, boot and bound dispatch: each door reads the sealed boot-capabilities document with one shared rule, prints install advice only when absence is established on every PATH entry or a valid document lacks a required verb, and names its exit code. README and CHANGELOG give a non-destructive upgrade order and say, before the upgrade step, that the copy earlier versions carried is removed and that anything still running it stops until it is pointed at a global install. Packaging tests fail on a reintroduced telepty dependency, lockfile entry, install script or root shrinkwrap, and on any command in the upgrade section other than the allowed installs and read-only reads. Also included are the release records: package version, lockfile, changelog, public projection, this file, the planning manifest, the security evidence blobs, the policy path and the workflow's security-policy pin. Limits: six independent reviews rejected successive wordings of the upgrade section and the last finding is stated as a known limit rather than removed (an upgrade can stop a host whose wrapper or service still runs the nested copy); the release repairs nothing on a host; versions 0.2.5 to 0.2.7 stay published as they are; Windows guidance is less verified than Linux and macOS. The maintainer accepted these residuals for this patch release on 2026-11-22.
